findings.finding: AC4 exercises the live code path (retype → review-plan reruns) but provides no concrete proving command — only prose ('running it on a scratch ticket and recording the runner/sidecar_emitted values on this ticket'). No `rebar` command sequence is shown, no assertion format is stated, and the criterion is not tagged `[operator-attested]` to make its manual-attestation nature explicit. As written, an executing agent cannot deterministically satisfy or verify this criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4: 'Retyping a ticket makes a subsequent review-plan actually run rather than replay'
scenarios: An executing agent cannot tell whether to run `rebar edit <id> --ticket_type=task && rebar review-plan <id>`, what the expected stdout looks like, or how to assert `runner != 'reused'`.
Without a concrete command, a reviewer cannot reproduce or validate the evidence recorded on the ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC4 verification clause with: 'verified by running `rebar edit <scratch-id> --ticket_type=task && rebar review-plan <scratch-id>` and confirming the output shows `runner: <value other than reused>` and `sidecar_emitted: true`; record the scratch ticket id and observed values here as attestation.' Add `[operator-attested]` tag if the `rebar` CLI is not available in CI.

tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1023: assert orchestrator.material_fingerprint(undeclared) == "8a2b6aa064e50d47"

findings.finding: `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` contains two hardcoded SHA assertions (`"8a2b6aa064e50d47"` and `"54fd84b5d3512772"` at lines 1023-1024) that call `orchestrator.material_fingerprint(...)` and will break when `ticket_type` is added to the `basis` dict, because the sha256 output changes for every context. The plan's Scope section names only `pass1.py` and `tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest.py` — `test_plan_review.py` is not listed as a file needing updates, so `make test` / `pytest` will fail after the change.
scenarios: `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_material_fingerprint_distinguishes_declared_none_without_legacy_churn` fails after the change because the golden hashes no longer match.

The AC verification command (`pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py`) passes but the broader `pytest` run fails, making the `make lint/typecheck/pytest` AC step misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add: '`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — update the two hardcoded SHA hex values in `test_material_fingerprint_distinguishes_declared_none_without_legacy_churn` to reflect the new hash output once `ticket_type` is included in the basis (or replace with inequality-only assertions that do not pin exact hex values).'

findings.finding: `material_fingerprint`'s affected-file inventory omits `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`, which contains hard-coded golden SHA-256 fingerprint values (`"8a2b6aa064e50d47"`, `"54fd84b5d3512772"`) that will break deterministically when `ticket_type` is added to the hash basis.
scenarios: tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_material_fingerprint_distinguishes_declared_none_without_legacy_churn fails with an AssertionError on the golden-value assertions (lines 1023–1024) after ticket_type is added, causing `make test` / CI to fail even though the production fix is correct — and the plan's own AC5 pytest invocation would not catch this because it excludes test_plan_review.py.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope section, add a bullet: `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — update or remove the two pinned golden-value assertions in `test_material_fingerprint_distinguishes_declared_none_without_legacy_churn` (lines 1023–1024); their hex values are computed from the pre-change basis and will be wrong after `ticket_type` is added. In AC5, extend the pytest invocation to include `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan to the Approach section (e.g., 'Revert this commit to restore the old fingerprint function; existing attestations will re-validate against the original hash and no re-reviews will be required').
evidence: Approach: 'That cost is accepted rather than engineered around, because it fails in the safe direction.'
Approach: 'every currently-certified attestation becomes stale on its next staleness check, and those tickets need one fresh review-plan before their next claim or close.'
ABSENCE: No section describes how to revert if the mass-invalidation causes operational problems (e.g., overwhelming review queue, deployment blocked by stale attestations across many tickets).
findings.finding: The plan acknowledges and justifies the destructive consequence (mass invalidation of all existing attestations) but provides no rollback or back-out plan. T4 requires an explicit reversibility mechanism, not only acknowledgement and justification.
scenarios: After deployment, the team finds that dozens of in-progress tickets now require re-review before they can be claimed or closed, blocking a release; there is no documented back-out path (e.g., revert the commit and re-deploy to restore old fingerprints).
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach: 'Rollback: reverting this commit restores the original `material_fingerprint` function and all existing attestation hashes will match again. No data migration is needed to roll back; the consequence is only that the retyping defect is restored.'
